title: Ember shift: rollout ops workpad and telemetry-shepherd checklist
content:
Purpose:
This workpad collects operational checklists, a staggered calendar, and an annotated draft of release notes for the Ember Shift rollout (small-phase rollout designed to reduce token-surge pressure during nightly backfills). The goal: get a compact, repeatable operating procedure we can run with a single on-call and one flight lead for the 02:00-06:00 PT night window.

Quick context / constraints:
- Target: introduce runtime changes that modify KV cache eviction heuristics and add a light-weight token-throttle to downstream routers.
- Risk profile: medium — low CPU but high potential tail-latency if kv eviction misbehaves.
- Traffic footprint: primary traffic is US-west region, expected 20% traffic reduction via traffic-shepherd for canary.
- Rollout window chosen for minimum user-visible impact: 02:00-06:00 PT on Nov 10–12, 2026.

Preflight checklist (48–24h):
- [ ] Feature flags created for: ember_eviction_v2 / ember_throttle_light / ember_telemetry_v1. Linear: RED-1234.
- [ ] Canary variant built and smoke-tested in staging (runtime PR: #4832).
- [ ] Perf bench: 1k concurrent sessions synthetic test with 4k token bursts. Baseline and candidate collected. Attach CSV to PR.
- [ ] Rollback knobs validated: auto-disable FF and hotpatch revert PR ready (author: @mariana).
- [ ] Pager rotations: alert routing updated to include ember-shift-responder list.
- [ ] Observability: dashboard created with these tiles: latency P50/P95/P99, kv-evict-rate, cache-hit-rate, throttled-requests, error-rate by route, pending-queue-length. Alert thresholds documented.
- [ ] Test prompts for quality regression: short prompt set (promptset: ember-smoke-12) and long-dialog set (ember-long-5).

Night-of quick runbook (02:00 PT baseline):
Phase A — micro-canary (02:00–02:45)
- Traffic split: 2% to canary variant (traffic-shepherd gate).
- Monitoring cadence: check dashboard at 5, 15, 30 minutes; call out to flight lead Slack channel with snapshot at 15m.
- Acceptance criteria: no >2x increase in P99; kv-evict-rate difference within expected ±15%; 0 new errors with code 5xx.
- If fail: immediate rollback flag set by flight lead and scale canary to 0%.

Phase B — phased expansion (02:45–04:00)
- If Phase A green, increase to 10% for 20m, then 30% for 20m, then 60% for 15m.
- At each step: validate P50/P95/P99 and token-throttle events (should be sparse).
- If small anomalies (degraded P99 but healthy P50): hold at current percent and triage for 30m, consider warm-up of cache by replaying sampled requests to canary nodes.

Phase C — full region ramp (04:00–05:00)
- Move to 100% for US-west; enable regional fallback policy so if latency increases we automatically route 25% to dedicated fallback cluster.
- Monitor for backpressure signals on upstream queues and autoscaler churn.

Phase D — stabilisation + bake (05:00–06:00)
- Keep at target for 60m, run quality spot-checks: ember-long-5 on prod canary path and compare to baseline.
- Capture final telemetry export for postmortem.

Operator notes / heuristics:
- KV eviction regression signature: sudden drop in cache-hit-rate with P95 rising >40ms with correlated increase in kv-evict-rate. Prefer rollback if P99 increases >25% from baseline for >10 minutes.
- Token-throttle tuning: light mode should only fire under sustained token-rate above configured threshold; spikes are acceptable if short (<30s).
- Use sampled request replays to warm caches — do not exceed 5% of normal request volume to avoid amplification.

Alerting and run closures:
- Critical alerts (pager): P99 latency > 2500ms for 5m, error-rate >1% for 5m, increased tail-queue-length.
- Non-critical (notify channel): kv-evict-rate > expected + 20% or throttle events > 50/min.
- Post-run checklist: collect traces (traces-export: ember-nightly-<date>.tgz), export metrics snapshot, attach final dashboards, add one-line summary to release notes.

Rollback playbook (fast and slow):
- Fast (immediate): flip ember_eviction_v2 FF -> off; scale canary to 0%. Announce in #release-ops with reason and initial diagnostics.
- Slow (investigate): if issue is degraded but non-critical, reduce traffic to 10% and enable cache-warm replay for 20m while investigating.

Annotated rollout calendar (compact):
- 2026-11-09 10:00 PT: Final smoke on staging (owner: Ethan).
- 2026-11-09 18:00 PT: Preflight brief and shift handoff (participants: flight lead, on-call, telemetry).
- 2026-11-10 02:00–06:00 PT: Ember Shift Day 1 (ops).
- 2026-11-11 02:00–06:00 PT: Ember Shift Day 2 (ops) — expansion candidate if Day1 stable.
- 2026-11-12 02:00–06:00 PT: Ember Shift Day 3 (ops) — final region-wide rollout.
- 2026-11-12 08:00 PT: Postmortem note draft due (owner: Priya).

Draft release notes (to be edited before public release):
- Title: Ember Shift: improved cache eviction and adaptive token-shepherding
- Summary: This release adjusts KV cache eviction heuristics to reduce unnecessary evictions for short-lived sessions and adds a lightweight token-shepherding throttle to smooth microburst token spikes. Expected benefit: lower overall token-cost per request and improved P95 latency for medium-length sequences.
- Impact: No change to API surface. May alter response latency for very large sequences in edge cases; fallback policies remain in place.
- Rollout plan: Incremental night-window rollout over 3 nights with automated canary and fallback.
- Known issues: In rare cases (long-tail workloads) cache warm-up can temporarily increase P99; we will monitor and have rollback prepared.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Finalize telemetry thresholds with SRE (cc: Nora). Suggested: P99 alert at 2.5s, kv-evict delta alert at +20%.
- [ ] Confirm conformance with Dedicated clusters (some DDs use different KV settings).
- [ ] Add additional sample prompts from product-team for smoke validation.
- [ ] Decide whether to include an explicit canary throttle (rate-limit by token/sec) or rely on router-level token-shepherd.

Postmortem template (if needed)
- Timeline: minute-granular activity log.
- Signals: metrics/dash snapshot, traces, sampled requests, incident timeline.
- Root cause analysis: change in eviction policy parameters -> cache churn -> tail amplification.
- Remediation: revert policy and bake new tuning, plus add automated warm replay during ramp.
- Follow-ups: create a small 'eviction simulator' PR to reproduce pathological eviction at scale.

Notes to self:
- Keep the ops instructions minimal and prescriptive; prefer simple binary decisions for flight lead (increase, hold, rollback).
- Avoid heavy coupling to dedicated autoscaler changes in this rollout — separate follow-on.

Attachments to add before final handoff:
- perf CSVs, PR link (#4832), linear plan (RED-1234), dashboard snapshot PNGs, smoke prompts file.
